title: Abba bar Marta, or Mart
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.
copyright: English translation and editorial notes © 2026 Joshua Waxman. All rights reserved.
paragraphs: Hyman considers it very likely that his father Minyomi was Rav Nachman’s colleague, as in Bava Metzia 66a, and his mother was called Marta; he was called after his mother because once a rabid dog bit him and she made him a golden tube, and he was healed, as in Yoma 84a.
Hyman states that he is always mentioned by these two names, except Beitzah 22b, where he is called by the name Bar Marta.

He was Rav Yehudah’s student, and through this he was saved from the Exilarch’s men, as in Shabbat 121b: he owed money to the Exilarch’s house; they brought him and were tormenting him. He spat (and it was Shabbat); the Exilarch said, “Bring a vessel and turn it over it.” He said to them: “You need not; thus said Rav Yehudah: Spittle — one treads on it unawares.” He said to them, “He is a Torah scholar; let him go.” Yevamot 120a relates that once he escaped from them by sticking a piece of wax with a rag on his nose, and he passed before them and they did not recognize him. Gittin 37b relates that he owed Rabbah money and brought it to him in the Sabbatical year; Rabbah did as the law requires and said, “I release it,” and Abba took the money and went away. When Abaye came to Rabbah he found him very sad; he told him what had happened. Abaye went to Abba and said to him: “Why, when Rabbah said to you, ‘I release it,’ did you not say to him, ‘Even so’?” Abba immediately went to Rabbah a second time and asked to repay him; when Rabbah said, “I release it,” he said to him, “Even so, take it from me,” and then Rabbah took the money from his hand according to the law. Moed Katan 26b relates that once he came to Rava’s house to comfort him over his dead, and Abba overturned the bed in order to give Rava the mourners’ meal; Rava said of him: “How senseless is this Torah scholar.” In Beitzah 22a we find that he asked Abaye and raised an objection to him.
And what we find of him in the Land of Israel, as in Gittin 29b with Rabbi Abbahu — Hyman suggests that this is Abba bar Binyamin, who lived in Arbel; see his entry.

notes.text: עמו גובתא דדהבא is read she made him a golden tube and כיומה as Yoma, as disclosed previously. להברות is the mourners’ meal. Hyman’s Minyomi father/Marta mother inference and alternative Palestinian Abba barBinyamin remain qualified, with both Rabbah the creditor and Rava the mourner retained.

The complete consulted Gittin 37b account explicitly equates Abba bar Marta with Abba bar Minyomi, makes Rabbah the creditor and has Abaye direct the renewed repayment with even so. It does not independently establish Hyman’s Minyomi-parent/Marta-mother reconstruction or his always-name assertion. Rabbah the creditor and Rava the mourner remain distinct; the possible Palestinian Abba bar Binyamin remains possible.
